research_goal: Build a defensible theoretical framework for publishing RAKL as a candidate scientific research method for LLM-mediated inquiry, while aggressively deduplicating prior art and freezing novelty falsifiers.
primary_claim: Candidate novelty lies in the integrated epistemic transition discipline, not its individual ingredients.
theory_falsifier: A pre-cutoff prior method semantically equivalent to the integrated RAKL control law refutes or narrows the method-level novelty claim.

validation.prior_active_behavior_validation: Round 008 validation recorded exact-candidate and post-promotion pytest results; this receipt does not relabel those prior runs as tests of Round 009 documentation.

saturation.reason: Six retained theory/publication objects survived deduplication and new novelty/process-benchmark fibers were opened.

next_ai.positive: If independent novelty review fails to find an integrated equivalent, narrow and preregister the surviving method-level claim before empirical headline experiments.
next_ai.null: If theory-specific ablations show no improvement on their registered process metrics, preserve the null and weaken the claim rather than adding post-hoc metrics.
next_ai.refuted: If a semantically equivalent prior method is found, preserve it as refuting evidence, update T001, and reposition RAKL as an implementation/extension or a narrower contribution.
next_ai.partial_id: If prior art covers only a subset or full-text access is incomplete, publish an explicit component-level novelty matrix and leave unknown cells unresolved.
next_ai.blocked: If a claim cannot be checked against full text/code or a proof obligation lacks enough formal definition, mark it BLOCKED/CANNOT_CHECK rather than infer novelty or validity.
next_ai.transport: Search/API/tooling failure creates no novelty credit and no scientific evidence; resume the same frozen claim registry without counting a new independent round.
